starter.index.html: To-Do List
starter.README.md:
# To-Do List

Build a note list from a version-one document with stable IDs. The two supplied notes make the initial state concrete. Complete addNote(state, value, id) and renderNotes(state) in script.js. addNote trims and validates a 1–200-character note, rejects a repeated ID or more than 100 records, pushes one {id, text} object and returns true. Use the supplied recordId and textField helpers. renderNotes creates a list item for each record and assigns its text with textContent. An empty array displays No notes.

The supplied form generates an ID once per accepted submission. Its transaction helper clones state, applies the mutation, validates the complete document and saves JSON before replacing working state. Trace this route in storage.js and the perform function. A failed save keeps the previous document. Invalid or unsupported stored JSON stays available for recovery and produces a read-only example.

Add two notes, including duplicate text, and refresh at the same origin. Each note must retain its own ID. Verify literal markup-shaped text, blank/overlength input, the record limit, failed saving and corrupted storage using CASES.md. This project supplies creation and rendering; deletion belongs to the next core project.

## Run and continue

Open index.html in a current browser. For stable origin-based persistence, an available Python 3 installation can serve this exported folder with: python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 . Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in that case. Direct file storage varies by browser;denied storage shows the read-only example. Keep the same origin and browser profile for refresh checks. IDE code exports contain the project files;localStorage is separate. Read storage.js and CASES.md before comparing the reference.

Complete addNote, renderNotes before comparing the reference.
starter.CASES.md:
# To-Do List cases

1. Add two notes;reload and compare text and IDs.
2. Duplicate note text retains distinct IDs.
3. Markup-shaped text stays text;blank,overlength and 101st note are rejected.
4. A failed setItem keeps both working state and stored JSON.
5. Invalid JSON,unsupported schema and denied storage retain recoverable data and show read-only state.
6. The base list has no Delete or completion controls;mobile and enlarged text reflow.

starter.README.md:
# Deleting Notes

Extend the completed local note list with deletion. Adding, validation, rendering and persistence are supplied from the earlier project. Complete deleteNote(state, id) in script.js. Find the note with the selected stable ID, remove exactly that record and return true. Return false for an unknown ID so no stored document is rewritten. Array positions describe display order; the stored ID identifies the record across changes.

Each Delete button captures its note's ID. After a successful transaction the renderer rebuilds the list and focus returns to the note input. The storage helper validates and saves a cloned document first, so a quota or policy failure leaves the previous state intact.

Delete the first, last and only note. Repeat a deletion with the removed ID, and try an ID that never existed. Add duplicate text to confirm the selected ID determines the deletion. Refresh after success and after a failed save. The list uses version one and has no completion checkbox; checking notes remains a separate optional project.

## Run and continue

Open index.html in a current browser. For stable origin-based persistence, an available Python 3 installation can serve this exported folder with: python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 . Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in that case. Direct file storage varies by browser;denied storage shows the read-only example. Keep the same origin and browser profile for refresh checks. IDE code exports contain the project files;localStorage is separate. Read storage.js and CASES.md before comparing the reference.

Complete deleteNote before comparing the reference.

starter.README.md:
# Checking Notes

Add persistent completion state to the local note list. Adding, deleting, safe rendering and the storage transaction are supplied. Complete upgradeLegacyNotes(value) and setCompletion(state, id, checked) in script.js.

Version two retains each note's ID and text and adds the Boolean done field. Upgrade a valid version-one document by preserving its records and assigning done: false. For the older string-array fixture, keep each valid nonblank note, including duplicate text, and assign a distinct legacy-position ID. Validate text and record limits and reject other shapes. Return the version-two document. The supplied normalizer validates the result and marks it as migrated; the next successful change saves that schema.

setCompletion finds one note by ID, accepts only a Boolean checked value, assigns its done field and returns true. Unknown IDs or non-Boolean values return false. The native checkbox and Completed/Incomplete text show the same state. Focus returns to the corresponding checkbox after rendering.

Use the two legacy fixtures in fixtures.js and CASES.md to verify migration, toggling one of two notes, repeated toggles, deletion after checking, refresh, corrupted data and failed saving. A failed migration preserves the original JSON for recovery. This is the optional extension of the two core note projects.

## Run and continue

Open index.html in a current browser. For stable origin-based persistence, an available Python 3 installation can serve this exported folder with: python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 . Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in that case. Direct file storage varies by browser;denied storage shows the read-only example. Keep the same origin and browser profile for refresh checks. IDE code exports contain the project files;localStorage is separate. Read storage.js and CASES.md before comparing the reference.

Complete upgradeLegacyNotes, setCompletion before comparing the reference.

starter.README.md:
# Message Board

Build a single-browser topic board with separate title, site URL and optional image-address fields. Complete addTopic(state, title, url, imageUrl, id) and renderTopics(state) in script.js. The supplied version-one fixture contains two topics with stable IDs and ordering values.

addTopic validates the ID, a 1–100-character title and the two addresses, then creates one post with a locally increasing order value. Reject repeated IDs and more than 30 topics. Use reviewedUrl for the explicit site/image origins in storage.js. An empty image address is valid and uses the supplied decorative illustration. A failed image load exposes a text fallback.

renderTopics sorts a copy by descending order, builds each article with DOM methods, assigns the title with textContent and links to its reviewed site URL. Assign image addresses through the img src property and handle load failure. The supplied transaction saves a validated clone before changing working state. Reset requires confirmation; read-only recovery preserves original saved bytes.

Create at least two new topics and check ordering, the three distinct fields, refresh, markup-shaped titles, disallowed URLs, image failure, record/document limits, corrupted storage and failed saving. Adding comments is a separate optional extension; this core board displays topics.

## Run and continue

Open index.html in a current browser. For stable origin-based persistence, an available Python 3 installation can serve this exported folder with: python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 . Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in that case. Direct file storage varies by browser;denied storage shows the read-only example. Keep the same origin and browser profile for refresh checks. IDE code exports contain the project files;localStorage is separate. Read storage.js and CASES.md before comparing the reference.

Complete addTopic, renderTopics before comparing the reference.

# Adding Comments

Extend the completed topic board with nested comments. Topic creation, URL validation, ordering, rendering, local transactions and a version-one upgrade are supplied. Complete addComment(state, postId, value, id) in script.js.

Find the parent topic by stable ID. An unknown parent returns false without changing or saving the document. Validate a unique comment ID and trimmed text of 1–400 characters. Append one {id, text} object to that topic's comments array, with at most 20 comments per topic and 200 across the board. The full document must remain within 128 KiB.

The renderer creates a labeled form for each topic and captures its ID. Adding a newer topic changes display positions while the captured ID still selects the intended parent. Duplicate comment text is allowed as distinct records. The supplied renderer uses textContent and restores focus to the appropriate new comment input.

Comment on two topics, add a newer topic, comment again on an older one and refresh. Verify stable associations, duplicate and markup-shaped text, blank/overlength input, missing parents, limits, reset and storage failures using CASES.md. A failed save preserves the previous document. Reset restores the supplied example and clears its comments. This project remains optional.

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in that case. Direct file storage varies by browser;denied storage shows the read-only example. Keep the same origin and browser profile for refresh checks. 7. Failed save and corrupt/unsupported storage preserve prior bytes.
8. All native labels,focus and enlarged-text controls remain usable.

readings.title: Local Documents and Stable IDs
readings.content:
A note has text and an identity. A stored document also needs a version so later code can recognize the shape it expects. The required projects keep their documents in this browser's local storage; the original hosted examples remain source references for the tasks.

## Worked document change

Start with two records:

```json
{"schemaVersion":1,"notes":[{"id":"note-a","text":"Sketch the layout."},{"id":"note-b","text":"Check the last case."}]}
```

Deleting `note-a` leaves `note-b` with the same ID and text. Its array position changes from one to zero. The delete button passes the stored ID to `deleteNote`; the function finds that record, removes it and returns `true`. An unknown ID returns `false` and leaves the document unchanged. The supplied transaction helper then validates and saves a changed document before replacing the working state.

A function argument named `state` is this data object. The browser's global `document` is the DOM object used to create elements and find controls. Keeping those names distinct prevents a data record from being mistaken for a page.

## Read, parse and validate

Storage values are strings. `JSON.stringify` turns a plain document into a JSON string; `JSON.parse` turns the stored string back into a value. Parsing can fail, and successful parsing still needs shape checks. A JSON number or an object with the wrong version is not a valid notes document.

The supplied validator requires version one, at most 100 notes, unique nonempty IDs and note text of 1–200 characters after trimming. It constructs fresh objects containing the expected fields. The storage helper also limits an encoded document to 128 KiB. Trace these checks in `storage.js` before implementing the starter's mutation and rendering functions.

## Commit one change

`commitDocument` clones the last valid state, passes the clone to the mutation function, validates it and serializes it. Only a successful `setItem` changes the working state. A quota or policy failure therefore leaves the previous state and saved document intact. The status explains the failure.

An unreadable, oversized or unsupported saved value stays in storage. A read-only example appears with the original JSON available for recovery. This is different from an empty store, which starts a new document. Verify both situations; replacing damaged data with an empty array would conceal a recoverable attempt.

## Render text and retain focus

Create a list item for each note and assign its text with `textContent`. Markup-shaped input then appears as text. The mutation works on state; the renderer builds the page from that state. Deleting a note returns focus to the note input, giving keyboard users a predictable continuation.

The first project implements adding and rendering. The second supplies those earlier functions and asks for deletion. The optional completion project supplies deletion and adds a checkbox state plus migration.

## Upgrade the schema

Version two adds a Boolean `done` field. Existing version-one objects retain their IDs and text while receiving `done: false`. The older string-array fixture needs IDs as well: derive distinct `legacy-0`, `legacy-1` and later IDs from the original positions, keeping duplicate text as separate notes. Blank strings can be omitted; valid strings remain. Reject an unsupported shape while preserving its raw value.

A successful completion change saves version two. Reopening then retains the IDs and completion values rather than running the migration again.

## Run and verify

Reload the same project location and browser profile to test persistence. Browser treatment of direct `file:` storage varies; a blocked store produces the read-only example. For consistent origin-based testing, serve the exported folder on loopback with an available static server, for example `python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1`, then open `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. A file URL and that HTTP origin have separate stores. An IDE code export carries the project files; browser storage is a separate result.

Use each project's `CASES.md` for the first, last, only, unknown-ID, repeated-delete, migration, refresh and failed-save cases. See the MDN references for [localStorage](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/localStorage), [setItem](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Storage/setItem) and [JSON parsing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse).

readings.title: Local Topics and Comments
readings.content: A board stores topics, and the optional extension stores comments inside their parent topics. Each object has an ID. The title, site URL and image address are separate fields because each serves a different purpose: naming the topic, opening its resource and illustrating it. ## Worked parent lookup Suppose topic `post-a` links to a drawing reference and topic `post-b` links to a field guide. Adding a newer topic changes their display positions. A comment form captures `post-a` when it is created, so submitting it still updates that topic after the list is reordered. ```js const post = state.posts.find(post => post.id === postId); if (!post) return false; post.comments.push({ id, text: textField(value, 400) }); ``` This excerpt shows the parent lookup and safe text normalization. The complete function also checks per-topic and whole-board comment limits and rejects a repeated comment ID. Two comments with the same text can be legitimate separate records. ## Model and validate the document The core document has `schemaVersion: 1` and a `posts` array. Each post contains `id`, `title`, `url`, `imageUrl` and `order`. The optional document uses version two and adds a `comments` array to every post. A version-one board can be upgraded by retaining its posts and adding empty comment arrays. The supplied validator accepts at most 30 topics, titles up to 100 characters and URLs up to 1,024 characters. Comments are limited to 400 characters, 20 per topic and 200 overall. The encoded document must also fit within 128 KiB; reaching any limit leaves the previous document intact. The order value increases when a topic is added. Render a sorted copy so newest topics appear first while their stored IDs remain stable. Keep comments attached to their parent objects throughout sorting and saving. ## Read addresses as URLs Use the supplied `reviewedUrl` helper to parse an address, check HTTPS, reject embedded credentials and compare its origin with a small explicit allowlist. Site links in these packs use example.com, MDN, English Wikipedia or the Fish and Wildlife Service. Image addresses use the Fish and Wildlife Service or Wikimedia raster-image hosts. Review the constants in `storage.js` before choosing an address. An empty image address uses the supplied decorative illustration. A failed image load displays a text fallback. A valid address can still fail to load, so creating the topic and handling its image are separate outcomes. The board remains usable when the image fails. Create anchors with DOM properties and titles/comments with `textContent`. An input such as `` should remain visible text. The URL field follows its own validation path; it does not become executable page content. ## Save before replacing state The shared transaction helper clones state, applies one mutation, validates the whole document and saves its JSON. A failed save preserves both the working document and the previous stored value. Read failures preserve the original bytes and show a read-only example with recovery text. The core starter implements topic creation and rendering. The comment starter supplies that earlier work and asks for a comment mutation. The form passes a captured topic ID to the mutation; a missing topic leaves the document unchanged. After a successful comment, restore focus to that topic's newly rendered input. ## Check the complete workflow Create two topics, add a newer one and comment on an older one. Refresh and verify the same association. Check duplicate text, whitespace-only input, overlength fields, foreign origins, unsupported schemas, storage denial and quota failure. Resetting a writable board requires confirmation and restores the supplied example, clearing its comments. The read-only recovery state preserves the saved bytes. Run the exported `index.html` in the tested browser or serve its folder on loopback as described in `README.md`. Keep the same origin for reload checks. These projects implement one browser's local board; multi-user synchronization requires a different server-backed design.
